_meta._owner: P1. The highest-leverage 45 minutes of the night (foray_plan.md §8).
_rules: The Diagnostician CLASSIFIES into these ids. It never invents a name.
'signals' are phrases in STUDENT language, not textbook language. That is what makes the classifier work, and what the offline fallback matches on.
'correction_hint' guides the Grounding Verifier - it still must find and cite a real MaterialChunk. The hint is never sent to the student on its own.
Do not write a misconception you cannot point at a page for. No page, no row.
_meta._planted: M12 is the demo spike: 23 of 60 students at week 6 on C11. Root cause traces C11 -> C10 -> C06 -> C05 -> C03.
_meta._calibration: When real classmate reflections arrive, steal their exact phrasing into 'signals'. That is free classifier calibration and costs nothing.

misconceptions.name: Thinks protocol layers are separate physical devices
misconceptions.correction_hint: layers are software abstractions in one host's stack, not separate boxes

misconceptions.name: Believes one header is added for the whole path
signals: it adds a header at the start
misconceptions.correction_hint: each layer adds its own header; the receiver strips them in reverse order

misconceptions.name: Believes one host can serve only one connection because it has one IP
signals: the server can only talk to one person
how does it handle two people with one address
misconceptions.correction_hint: the IP identifies the host; the four-tuple distinguishes simultaneous connections

misconceptions.name: Confuses port numbers with operating-system process IDs
signals: the OS assigns the port like a process
misconceptions.correction_hint: a port is a transport-layer identifier bound by a socket, unrelated to the OS pid

misconceptions.name: Thinks the server uses one socket for every client
signals: the server has a single socket
misconceptions.correction_hint: the welcoming socket accepts; each accepted connection gets its own socket

misconceptions.name: Believes UDP has no error detection at all
misconceptions.correction_hint: UDP does carry a checksum; what it lacks is recovery, not detection

misconceptions.name: Thinks a checksum guarantees the data is correct
signals: checksum proves the data is fine
misconceptions.correction_hint: a checksum detects likely errors probabilistically; it cannot guarantee correctness

misconceptions.name: Thinks Go-Back-N retransmits only the lost packet
signals: only the missing packet is sent again
misconceptions.correction_hint: GBN retransmits the lost packet and everything after it; Selective Repeat resends only the lost one

misconceptions.name: Thinks the MSS includes the TCP header
misconceptions.correction_hint: MSS is the maximum application-layer data, excluding TCP/IP headers

misconceptions.name: Believes the receive window is a fixed constant
misconceptions.correction_hint: rwnd is advertised in every ACK and changes as the receiver's buffer drains

misconceptions.name: Thinks slow start is slow
signals: it starts slowly and stays slow
misconceptions.correction_hint: slow start begins small but grows exponentially — it is the fastest-growing phase

misconceptions.name: Believes a TCP connection is identified by the destination port alone
signals: the server can only have one connection on that port
each connection needs its own port number
two people can't connect to the same port
the port is basically the connection
misconceptions.correction_hint: a TCP socket is identified by a four-tuple: source IP, source port, destination IP, destination port

misconceptions.name: Thinks the three-way handshake carries the application data
signals: the request is sent in the SYN
three packets and the file is transferred
misconceptions.correction_hint: the handshake establishes state and initial sequence numbers; data follows afterwards

misconceptions.name: Thinks a port number identifies the host rather than the socket
signals: the port tells you which computer
misconceptions.correction_hint: the IP address identifies the host; the port identifies the process/socket on that host

misconceptions.name: Treats UDP as a broken or incomplete version of TCP
signals: UDP is TCP without the good parts
misconceptions.correction_hint: UDP is a deliberate choice: no handshake, no connection state, finer application control over what is sent and when

misconceptions.name: Believes TCP guarantees delivery to the application under all conditions
misconceptions.correction_hint: TCP guarantees reliable, in-order delivery only while the connection survives; it cannot deliver across a broken connection

misconceptions.name: Thinks sequence numbers count segments rather than bytes
signals: each packet increases the number by one
the sequence number is the packet number
misconceptions.correction_hint: TCP sequence numbers count bytes in the stream, not segments

misconceptions.name: Conflates flow control with congestion control
signals: the window stops the network overloading
flow control is because the internet is busy
misconceptions.correction_hint: flow control (rwnd) protects the receiver's buffer; congestion control (cwnd) protects the network
